reading.body:
A data center listed in Deer Valley, Arizona cannot be confirmed to exist, and its coordinates resolve to a garage door company.

The record carries no megawatts, no operator, no website, and no business registration. A reverse geocode of the stored coordinates returns A1 Garage Door Service at 2501 West Behrend Drive, an unrelated home-services business. The name Accelera Data Systems is generic enough that it does not by itself describe a colocation provider or hosting business. The most likely explanations are a stale or imprecise map pin, or an address that has since been vacated.

This matters because facility counts are only as good as their weakest entries. Arizona has four facilities with published power figures totaling 512 MW, and this site contributes nothing to that total because nothing about it has been verified. A count that includes unconfirmed rows overstates the infrastructure, and an overstatement of available capacity is exactly the kind of error that distorts any assessment of where compute can actually be built.

The data does not show that a data center was planned here and cancelled, nor that one operates under another name. It shows only that one map node, tagged as a facility, failed every check applied to it. The site sits roughly 15 to 20 miles from the other rows in its batch, so no shared building connects them either.
